source_text: etsi eos negatis attrahere quod in baptismo remittatur originale peccatum, tamen illo regenerationis lavacro adoptari ex filiis hominum in Dei filios non negatis, immo etiam praedicatis
pass_a_gloss: Even if you deny that they draw what is remitted in baptism as original sin, nevertheless you do not deny, indeed you even proclaim, that by that washing of regeneration they are adopted from being sons of human beings into being sons of God.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Augustine says that the authors deny that infants inherit original sin needing remission in baptism. They nevertheless affirm, and indeed proclaim, that the washing of rebirth adopts them from being children of human beings into being children of God (Titus 3:5; John 1:12–13; Romans 8:15).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
